in: A service-side reader for the five files (roadmap, feature registry, backlog active + terminal, build history + archived count) with the payload envelope of the earlier product, field for field: schema_version, generated_at, current_build, current_track, progress_contract, overall_progress_percent, current_track_progress_percent, tracks, now_next, roadmap_notes, backlog, backlog_counts, completed_features, build_history, archived_build_count, metadata_warnings. A missing or unreadable file yields its empty default and a metadata warning; it never fails the request.

The arithmetic, exactly: FEATURE percent = 100 if status is done when the feature has no criteria, else 0; with criteria, the sum of weights of criteria whose state is literally 'done' over the sum of all criterion weights, times 100, rounded to one decimal; a weight defaults to 1, is coerced to at least 0, and a non-numeric weight becomes 1. TRACK percent = the weighted mean of its features' percents by feature weight, over only the features whose ids the track lists and which exist in the registry. OVERALL percent = the same weighted mean over the tracks, by TRACK weight (not feature count). An empty denominator is 0. done_features counts features whose status is exactly 'done'.

The metadata warnings, all of them: unknown status or criterion state, duplicate feature ids, a track feature id with no feature, an undeclared current track, a current build absent from history, and the six cross-file rules -- the now horizon's build equals the newest build-history record; current_build equals the now horizon's build; an id that is both a feature and a build carries one canonical status; the next horizon is not already terminal; an open decision has a non-empty decide_by; a backlog item is not planned while its feature has started and a feature is not planned while its backlog item is done.

GET /project-plan returning that payload, gated as a read for any authenticated session (PO-NAV-5: visible to everyone today, administration-only later; do not simulate the future restriction). Service tests over fixture JSON files, including the arithmetic against hand-computed expectations and each warning rule firing.

The screen, reproducing the earlier layout in the product's own Material 3 components: three hero cards (declared roadmap completion with its bar and the caption that this is acceptance-criterion completion and not a time estimate; current major track with its progress contract; open backlog count with a chip per status); now / next / upcoming; major tracks as cards, the current one marked, each with a collapsible feature map; backlog and technical debt grouped by category, a group expanded when it holds a P0 or an in_progress row, each row showing priority, status, target and note; completed features with summary, why it matters and validated evidence; build history with the archived count; and the warning block followed by the roadmap notes. Category is an opaque grouping key, never an enum. No role-conditional rendering.

Two earlier defects are fixed and named in the SESSION_CLOSE rather than reproduced: the open-backlog hero counted every item whose status was not 'done', which counts deferred and validated items as open -- use the terminal set (done, automated_validated, real_env_validated, deferred) instead; and completed features were sorted by their introduced string lexically -- sort by parsed order with a documented fallback for unparseable values.
Frontend tests for the hero numbers, the grouping and expansion rule, and the warning block.
